title: How the Berlin Wall Worked
summary: Josh and Chuck explain how the Berlin Wall came to be and how it worked. They cover the end of World War Two and the division of Germany and Berlin into zones, the Soviet-controlled East versus the Western-held West Berlin island, the 1948-49 Berlin Airlift, the mass defections that led to the overnight construction of the wall on August 13, 1961, its evolution into a fortified multi-layered barrier with a death strip, guard towers and tunnels, notable deaths including Peter Fechter, and the 1980s reform era (glasnost, the Sinatra Doctrine, Hungary opening its Austrian border) that led to the wall's fall on November 9, 1989 and German reunification. The episode closes with listener mail about a best-day story and a few off-topic recommendations.

segments.title: Opening banter and the wall's basic facts
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the episode and the Berlin Wall, discuss the Wall's relief to some world leaders, and note the confirmed death toll of 136 with estimates ranging from 98 to 300.

segments.title: End of World War Two and division of Germany
segments.summary: After Germany surrendered, the Soviet Union joined the Allies against Germany, then the Allies divided Germany into four zones, with the Soviets forming the German Democratic Republic in their zone and the Western zones forming West Germany.

segments.title: Iron Curtain and the divided city of Berlin
segments.summary: The Soviets occupied and isolated Eastern Bloc countries behind the Iron Curtain, while Berlin, inside East Germany, was split into Soviet-controlled East Berlin and the Western-controlled island of West Berlin.

segments.title: Berlin Airlift
segments.summary: The Soviets blockaded rail and road access to West Berlin, and the Allies responded with the Berlin Airlift, flying in more than two hundred thousand tons of cargo a month at peak for almost a year until the blockade was lifted.

segments.title: Defections and the brain drain
segments.summary: Mass emigration from East Germany to West Berlin, mostly by young professionals and doctors, strained both sides and increased tensions, with more than two hundred thousand East Germans leaving.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: A break in the episode before the discussion of the wall's construction.

segments.title: Overnight construction of the wall on August 13, 1961
segments.summary: On the night of August 12-13, 1961, East German forces closed border crossings and began building a barbed wire and concrete barrier through central Berlin, catching many families and couples on opposite sides; the first generation wall was crude, built from bricks and mortar.

segments.title: Physical design of the wall and the death strip
segments.summary: The fortified wall had concrete and rebar sections, guard towers, tank traps, barbed wire, a death strip with chemicals and guard dogs, raked sand to show footprints, and a white painted east face; guards were screened for West German ties.

segments.title: Crossings, standoffs and border travel
segments.summary: West Germans could travel into East Germany with special plates, and in 1961 a tank standoff occurred at Checkpoint Charlie. The hosts also discuss the names of the other checkpoints.

segments.title: Escape attempts, deaths and the completed wall
segments.summary: Stories of escape attempts include apartments straddling the wall, windows bricked up, a 76-year-old woman pulled from a window, the 1962 shooting of Peter Fechter, and tunnel escapes; the wall was fully completed by 1963.

segments.title: Glasnost, the Sinatra Doctrine and the fall of the wall
segments.summary: Gorbachev's glasnost and the Sinatra Doctrine led Hungary to open its Austrian border, New Forum protests grew, and on November 9, 1989 East Germany announced open travel, and crowds tore down the wall; the hosts note the subsequent reunification.

segments.title: Listener mail: best day story and closing
segments.summary: A listener shares a best-day story about a childhood cat drowning and a classmate who held her hand; the hosts close with contact information and a question about casting a film.
